_meta.description: Document-rules config for pil — Public Interest Litigation under Article 226 (HC) / Article 32 (SC). For matters affecting public interest by a representative petitioner. Locus standi liberalised per S.P. Gupta and Hussainara Khatoon.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. S.P. Gupta, Hussainara Khatoon, BALCO frivolous-PIL cost cites mandatory.

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, the Petitioner herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to my personal knowledge save and except such facts as are gathered from documents, research, reports and sources stated, which I believe to be true and accurate. I further verify that I have no personal interest in the subject matter of this petition and the present petition is being filed bona fide in the larger public interest. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a Public Interest Litigation petition. PIL is a procedural innovation, not a substantive right — locus standi liberalised but discipline strict.
Cause-title MUST include 'In the matter of' format identifying the public interest subject.
Para 1: Description of parties.

Para 2: Petitioner credentials — public-spirited person; track record; not a busybody. Cite S.P. Gupta v. Union of India 1981 Supp SCC 87 (locus liberalised); People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India (1982) 3 SCC 235; Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984) 3 SCC 161.

Para 3: No personal interest declaration — per State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal (2010) 3 SCC 402, mandatory disclosure: (i) petitioner's credentials, (ii) source of information, (iii) personal interest if any, (iv) source of funding, (v) why locus.
Para 4: Source of funding — disclose. PILs by anonymous funders viewed with suspicion.
Para 5: Public interest element — section of public affected (disadvantaged, poor, marginalised, public at large). Show it is not private grievance dressed as PIL.

Para 6-8: Factual basis — research, RTI replies, news reports, expert literature, surveys, photographs. PIL must be backed by serious data, not bare allegations. Cite Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (1996) 3 SCC 212; M.C. Mehta line of cases.

Para 9: Constitutional rights at stake — Articles 14, 19, 21 (expanded — Right to clean environment Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) 1 SCC 598; Right to health Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity v. State of WB (1996) 4 SCC 37; Right to education Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) 3 SCC 666). DPSP: Articles 38, 47, 48A.
Para 10: Alternative remedy position — statutory authority approached and failed; OR none adequate.
Para 11: Reliefs sought — specific, precise. Vague PILs dismissed.
Para 12: Frivolity safeguard:
- Cite State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal (2010) 3 SCC 402 — HC must lay down rules (most HCs have done so);
- Cite BALCO Employees' Union v. Union of India (2002) 2 SCC 333 — costs for frivolous PIL (₹1 lakh+);
- Cite Holicow Pictures Pvt Ltd v. Prem Chandra Mishra (2007) 14 SCC 281 — publicity-interest litigation discouraged;
- Cite Ashok Kumar Pandey v. State of WB (2004) 3 SCC 349 — PILs cannot be allowed to be misused.

Para 13: For environmental PIL — precautionary principle, polluter pays — Cite Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996) 5 SCC 647; M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997) 1 SCC 388 (public trust doctrine).
Para 14: For prison / criminal justice PIL — Cite Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1980) 1 SCC 81 (right to speedy trial / undertrials); Sunil Batra; Khatri v. State of Bihar (1981) 1 SCC 627.

Para 15: Where continuing mandamus / expert committee sought — Cite Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1998) 1 SCC 226 (continuing mandamus); MC Mehta line (Bhure Lal Committee for vehicular pollution).
Prayer — precise reliefs; direction for committee where complex factual investigation needed.
Affidavit by petitioner-in-person or authorised office bearer (with board resolution annexed).
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Life, dignity, environment, health, education — expanded reading
DPSP — promote social order securing welfare
DPSP — duty to raise standard of nutrition and health

filing_checklist: Petition (original + copies per HC PIL Rules; SC: per applicable order)
Affidavit in support (mandatory) — disclosing Balwant Singh Chaufal mandates
Vakalatnama (if represented; in-person allowed with permission)
Petitioner credentials documents (registration certificate / bye-laws / track record)
Research documents, RTI replies, expert reports, news clippings
Photographs, surveys, scientific reports (for environmental / health PIL)
Documents of representation to authorities and their replies
Court fee per HC schedule (some HCs grant fee waiver for bona fide PIL)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: petitioner_name and petitioner_type must not be empty
constitutional_rights_at_stake must have at least one selected
reliefs_sought must not be empty and must be specific
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
Court level limited to HC or SC
